evidence.excerpt: The scarcity of labeled defect images is a persistent bottleneck in training robust visual quality control models, particularly for rare or newly introduced defect types. This paper explores procedural and generative approaches to synthetic defect generation, proposing a unified pipeline that combines physically based rendering (PBR) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) fine-tuned on a small set of real defect exemplars. The pipeline produces photorealistic defect images across six categories—scratches, pits, cracks, stains, delamination, and inclusion—on both metallic and polymer substrates. A systematic evaluation protocol measures the downstream impact of synthetic augmentation on detection model performance using three standard industrial datasets. Models trained with a 70% synthetic / 30% real mixture achieve accuracy within 3.2% of fully supervised baselines trained on complete real datasets, while reducing annotation effort by approximately 80%. The study also benchmarks the realism of generated images using FID and a domain-expert perceptual rating study. The findings support synthetic data generation as a cost-effective strategy for bootstrapping quality control systems in low-data manufacturing environments.
